identity.title: The Impact of Silicate Grain Coagulation on Millimeter Emission from Massive Protostellar Disks

paper_type_evidence.quote: we aim to reproduce the observed radial profile of the $1.14$-$\mathrm{mm}$ continuum emission from the massive protostellar disk around GGD27-MM1, as reported by (cite: Anez+2020).

evidence.quote: The source distance is $d = 1.4{\rm\:kpc}$
The source distance is $d = 1.4{\rm\:kpc}$

question.value: How does silicate grain coagulation affect (sub-)mm emission from hot massive protostellar disks, and what fragmentation velocity does the GGD27-MM1 1.14 mm profile imply?

evidence.quote: the present study aims to self-consistently constrain both the coagulation properties of silicate grains and the parameters reproducing the overall $1.14\:\mathrm{mm}$ continuum emission.
which made use of ALMA data (ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00480.S)
which value is the same as the previous ALMA Band 6 observations of the GGD27-MM1 disk

angular_resolution.value: beam FWHM sqrt(45.0 mas x 38.3 mas)

evidence.quote: the observation beam has a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of $\sqrt{45.0{\rm\:mas} \times 38.3{\rm\:mas}}$

what.value: Radial profile of 1.14 mm dust continuum intensity (Figure 7, 16 points, r=0-220 au), corrected for compact ionized source

evidence.quote: specifically Figure 7, which presents the radial profile of dust continuum intensity observed at $1.14{\rm\:mm}$.

what.value: Polarization at 1.14 mm: P=1-1.5% in SW disk at ~100 au

evidence.quote: the polarization vectors align with the disk minor axis with polarization degrees of $P=1$–$1.5\:\%$

what.value: Stellar luminosity 1.4e4 Lsun from IR observations

evidence.quote: The stellar luminosity is set at $L=1.4\times10^4\:L_\odot$, estimated from near, mid and far -infrared observations

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Steady disk model with single-size dust growth/fragmentation, plus analytic scattering radiative transfer for non-isothermal slab; astronomical silicate opacities

evidence.quote: we introduce a new analytical solution for radiative transfer that assumes isotropic scattering, allowing us to calculate the emergent intensity while incorporating the vertical temperature gradient of the disk.
The disk model used in this study is primarily based on that developed by (cite: Yamamuro2023).
Following (cite: Kataoka2015), we adopt $C = 2\:\%$.

what.value: Analytic RT derivation deferred to forthcoming paper

evidence.quote: The detailed derivation of this analytical solution, along with a discussion of its accuracy, will be presented in a forthcoming paper (Tanaka et al., in prep.).

unstated_but_needed: Digitized values of the Anez-Lopez et al. 2020 Figure 7 profile and its uncertainties
Disk inclination and position angle values used
Full derivation of the analytic RT solution (in prep.)
Optool settings (e.g. grain size grid) and the exact radial sampling of NMSE

analysis_steps.goal: Build disk structure with grain growth

method.value: Steady disk integrated inward from r_disk to 10 au with single-size dust growth/fragmentation

evidence.quote: In this study, we stop the calculations at an inner radius of $10{\rm\:au}$.

key_parameters.value: M=20 Msun, L=1.4e4 Lsun, alpha_floor=0.01, f_dg=0.01

evidence.quote: We take $\alpha_\mathrm{floor}=0.01$

assumptions.value: a_max=0.1 um at the disk outer edge

evidence.quote: We adopt the maximum grain radius of $a_\mathrm{max}=0.1\:\mathrm{\mu m}$ at the outer edge of the disk as the boundary condition.

method.value: Optool for compact spherical astronomical silicate with power-law size distribution

evidence.quote: The grain size distribution is assumed to follow a power law with an exponent of $-3.5$
the minimum grain radius is set to $a_{\rm min}=0.1{\rm\:\mu m}$
we replace the scattering opacity with the effective value for isotropic scattering

method.value: Analytic emergent intensity for vertically non-isothermal slab with scattering; project to sky and Gaussian smooth

evidence.quote: we apply Gaussian smoothing
the smoothing standard deviation is set to $\sigma_{\rm sm}=d\:{\rm FWHM}/(2\sqrt{2\log2})=58{\rm\:au}$

assumptions.value: radially symmetric beam; I=0 for r>r_disk

evidence.quote: our Gaussian smoothing uses a radially symmetric beam, ignoring the elliptical shape and position angle of the actual observation beam.

method.value: Minimize NMSE between model and observed major-axis profile over Mdot, r_disk, v_frag (plus a_lim or L), subject to a_max=100-150 um at r=90-110 au from polarization

evidence.quote: We identify candidate models by minimizing the normalized mean squared error (NMSE) between the observed and modeled intensity profiles.

key_parameters.value: Grid: Mdot 1e-5 to 1e-3 (20 log steps), r_disk 150-200 au, v_frag 0.1-30 m/s (30 log steps)

evidence.quote: We identify candidate models by minimizing the normalized mean squared error (NMSE) between the observed and modeled intensity profiles.

validation.value: Inner-disk mismatch compared to observations (20-30% fiducial; 8% and 6% for alternatives)

evidence.quote: where the discrepancy with observations is reduced to an average of $8\:\%$, compared to the $20$–$30\:\%$ mismatch in the fiducial case.

used_for.value: Dust opacities and scattering matrix elements

evidence.quote: we utilize the optical properties of dust grains derived by `Optool`
$v_\mathrm{frag}=14\:\mathrm{m\:s^{-1}}$
$\dot{M}_\mathrm{gas}=1\times10^{-3}\:M_\odot \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$
$v_\mathrm{frag}=17\:\mathrm{m\:s^{-1}}$, $\dot{M}_\mathrm{gas}=7.9\times10^{-4}\:M_\odot \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, $r_\mathrm{disk}=150\:\mathrm{au}$, and $L=7\times10^4\:L_\odot$.
the fragmentation velocity consistently falls within the range of $v_\mathrm{frag}=12$–$17{\rm\:m\:s^{-1}}$
enhanced scattering dims the disk emission by $20$–$30\:\%$ relative to the blackbody emission

findings_qualitative.value: Silicate fragmentation velocity ~15 m/s is below typical maximum collision velocities (20-50 m/s) in protoplanetary disks, so collisional growth alone is unlikely to form rocky planetesimals.

evidence.quote: suggesting that collisional coagulation alone is insufficient for silicate dust to form rocky planetesimals in such environments.

claims.hypothesis: Grain growth beyond lambda/2pi dims inner-disk 1.14 mm emission
claims.experiment: Radiative transfer of self-consistent disk model
claims.result: Brightness falls up to 20-30% below surface blackbody
claims.finding: Scattering dimming is a signature of grain evolution

evidence.quote: enhanced scattering dims the disk emission by $20$–$30\:\%$

claims.experiment: NMSE grid search with polarization grain size constraint

evidence.quote: the fragmentation velocity consistently falls within the range of $v_\mathrm{frag}=12$–$17{\rm\:m\:s^{-1}}$

claims.result: Inner region >20% too dim in all models
claims.finding: Need grain-size limit or higher luminosity

evidence.quote: the inner region consistently exhibits intensities that are more than $20\:\%$ lower than the observed values

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Anez-Lopez et al. settling assumption deemed unlikely given St/alpha<<1

evidence.quote: significant vertical settling is unlikely because the condition ${\rm St}/\alpha \ll 1$ holds in this regime.

limitations_admitted.value: Polarization may arise from aligned grains rather than self-scattering, making v_frag highly uncertain

evidence.quote: we cannot rule out the possibility that the polarization may instead result from the alignment of elongated grains
